Duration::microseconds¶

Back to Duration API Reference

Signature¶

Series Duration::microseconds() const

The Microsecond Field¶

microseconds() returns the three decimal digits below the millisecond field, in the range 0..999. It is the middle subsecond component, not all microseconds elapsed since the beginning of the second. Thus 0.005006007 seconds yields millisecond 5, microsecond 6, and nanosecond 7.

Use total().microseconds() for a complete unit conversion. Component extraction remains integer-exact and never passes through floating point. For negative durations, floor normalization keeps this field nonnegative: -1 ns is represented with microsecond field 999.

Result Contract¶

The returned Int64 Series has the receiver’s exact shape and owns its storage. NaT maps to Duration::kNaT; empty shapes remain defined and empty. The method performs one O(numel) pass and leaves the Duration unchanged.

Examples¶

Example 1. Select the microsecond digits from a nanosecond-exact value.

std::cout << pluss::series::print(
    pluss::duration::nanos(93'784'005'006'007LL).microseconds());

Output¶

Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=6

Example 2. The field remains within 0..999 for negative spans.

constexpr std::int64_t hour = 3'600'000'000'000LL;
constexpr std::int64_t day = 86'400'000'000'000LL;
std::cout << pluss::series::print(
    pluss::duration::nanos({-1, -hour, -day}).microseconds());

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[999, 0, 0]

Example 3. N-D shape and NaT identity are lane-preserving.

auto values = pluss::duration::nanos(
    {93'784'005'006'007LL, pluss::Duration::kNaT, -1, 0}, {2,2});
std::cout << pluss::series::print(values.microseconds());

Output¶

Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=
⎡   6 -9223372036854775808 ⎤
⎣ 999                    0 ⎦

Example 4. Zero cardinality preserves all three axes.

std::cout << pluss::series::print(
    pluss::duration::zeros({2,0,3}).microseconds());

Output¶

Series(shape=[2,0,3], strides=[0,3,1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=0, contiguous=true)
[]

See Also¶

  • milliseconds(): the preceding fractional field.

  • nanoseconds(): the remaining sub-microsecond field.

  • total().microseconds(): complete elapsed microseconds.
